Investors often turn to recommendations made by Wall Street analysts before making a Buy, Sell, or Hold decision about a stock. While media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm employed (or sell-side) analysts often affect a stock's price, do they really matter?

Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB).

Airbnb currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.93, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 42 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.93 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 42 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 21 are Strong Buy and four are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 50% and 9.5% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for ABNB
Broker Rating Breakdown Chart for ABNB

Check price target & stock forecast for Airbnb here>>>

While the ABR calls for buying Airbnb, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential.

Do you wonder why? As a result of the vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover, their analysts tend to rate it with a strong positive bias. According to our research, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations for every "Strong Sell" recommendation.

In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

ABR Should Not Be Confused With Zacks Rank

Although both Zacks Rank and ABR are displayed in a range of 1--5, they are different measures altogether.

Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Is Airbnb (ABNB) a Solid Growth Stock? 3 Reasons to Think "Yes"

Investors seek growth stocks to capitalize on above-average growth in financials that help these securities grab the market's attention and produce exceptional returns. However, it isn't easy to find a great growth stock.

In addition to volatility, these stocks carry above-average risk by their very nature. Also, one could end up losing from a stock whose growth story is actually over or nearing its end.

However, the task of finding cutting-edge growth stocks is made easy with the help of the Zacks Growth Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which looks beyond the traditional growth attributes to analyze a company's real growth prospects.

Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB) is on the list of such stocks currently recommended by our proprietary system. In addition to a favorable Growth Score, it carries a top Zacks Rank.

Studies have shown that stocks with the best growth features consistently outperform the market. And returns are even better for stocks that possess the combination of a Growth Score of A or B and a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) or 2 (Buy).

While there are numerous reasons why the stock of this company is a great growth pick right now, we have highlighted three of the most important factors below:

Earnings Growth

Earnings growth is arguably the most important factor, as stocks exhibiting exceptionally surging profit levels tend to attract the attention of most investors. And for growth investors, double-digit earnings growth is definitely preferable, and often an indication of strong prospects (and stock price gains) for the company under consideration.

While the historical EPS growth rate for Airbnb is 22.4%, investors should actually focus on the projected growth. The company's EPS is expected to grow 36.2% this year, crushing the industry average, which calls for EPS growth of 27.3%.

Impressive Asset Utilization Ratio

Asset utilization ratio -- also known as sales-to-total-assets (S/TA) ratio -- is often overlooked by investors, but it is an important indicator in growth investing. This metric exhibits how efficiently a firm is utilizing its assets to generate sales.

Right now, Airbnb has an S/TA ratio of 0.55, which means that the company gets $0.55 in sales for each dollar in assets. Comparing this to the industry average of 0.52, it can be said that the company is more efficient.

While the level of efficiency in generating sales matters a lot, so does the sales growth of a company. And Airbnb is well positioned from a sales growth perspective too. The company's sales are expected to grow 17.3% this year versus the industry average of 3.7%.

We just published a list of the 10 Stocks Analysts Just Upgraded and Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) ranked 9th on this list.

Wall Street spent last Thursday reminding investors how quickly a favorite theme can turn. Worries that Democratic midterm wins could bring tighter rules for artificial intelligence and data centers sent technology stocks sharply lower. The damage spread well beyond the group that was under the microscope.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52%, its biggest one-day drop in 19 months, and closed more than 10% below its October record, a slide that put it in a correction. The S&P 500 lost 4.36%, its worst drop since the April 2025 tariff shock, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 3.44%. The drop more than erased the previous day's gain, the market's best in three months.

Trading was frantic. About 26.9 billion shares changed hands, against a 20-session average of 17.7 billion.

Chip Stocks Take the Heaviest Hit as AI Build-Out Fears Spread

Semiconductor stocks absorbed the worst of it, and the selling was heavy in the other stocks tied to data center spending too. Even so, the S&P 500 was still up 7.4% for the year, and the Nasdaq Composite was still up 4.6%.

"This feels like the capitulation phase for the data center capex beneficiary stocks, especially the semiconductors," Argent Capital Management portfolio manager Jed Ellerbroek told Reuters. The selling landed on top of a tightening cycle. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin both hinted at possible future rate hikes. Traders expected the Federal Reserve to raise rates again next month after a September increase.

Energy prices added to the strain. Brent crude rose 3.9% to $98.29 a barrel, while the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.83% from 4.90%. Readers who follow analyst calls on value can find more ideas in our list of affordable stocks that Wall Street analysts like.

Overseas, the Bank of England raised its main rate for the first time in three years. Governor Andrew Bailey said, "The best thing that can happen is to resolve the conflict in the Middle East; there's no question about it."

Investing.com — Online travel platforms historically moved in tandem with broader consumer discretionary spending, but recent market action highlights sharp valuation divergence across the sector. While Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) commands premium multiples above 30 times earnings and Morgan Stanley reiterated Booking Holdings (NASDAQ:BKNG) as its top industry pick, Expedia Group (NASDAQ:EXPE) has retreated to $259.24—trading near 12 times forward earnings despite delivering a third-quarter earnings beat.

That valuation discount does not reflect operational deterioration. Third-quarter revenue rose 12% year-over-year, supported by $3.7 billion in trailing twelve-month free cash flow and a high-margin enterprise partner division expanding at more than 20% annually. Yet despite generating consistent cash flow and retiring shares at an aggressive pace, Wall Street continues to price the company like an unhedged cyclical operator.

Spotting when steady, cash-generative market leaders trade at steep cyclical discounts is what InvestingPro's ProPicks AI models look for. The system maintains Expedia inside the Beat the S&P 500 strategy's active November portfolio, pairing the travel marketplace with high-conviction large caps—including a commercial aircraft turbine manufacturer, an entertainment streaming leader, and a biopharmaceutical developer with a commercial oncology franchise.

Running the travel desk behind banks and airlines

Expedia Group is best known for its consumer platforms—Expedia, Hotels.com, and Vrbo—but its most durable operational catalyst operates behind the scenes. Its B2B enterprise division supplies hotel, flight, and specialized travel inventory to more than 70,000 corporate partners, powering private-label booking tools for financial institutions, airlines, and corporate travel desks. In the second quarter, B2B revenue rose 23% year-over-year to $1.49 billion—marking the segment's 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth—and is projected to account for more than 45% of total corporate revenue by 2027.

The consumer-facing ecosystem has seen structural upgrades as well. Over the past 18 months, management migrated all disparate consumer brands onto a single, unified technology infrastructure, while its One Key loyalty network surpassed 90 million active members. Internal efficiency gains kept overhead expenses flat in the second quarter despite a 14% revenue expansion, while recent commercial acquisitions of Tiqets and CarTrawler expanded partner offerings into higher-margin activities and car rentals.

Have you looked into how Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB) performed internationally during the quarter ending September 2026? Considering the widespread global presence of this company, examining the trends in international revenues is essential for assessing its financial resilience and prospects for growth.

The global economy today is deeply interlinked, making a company's engagement with international markets a critical factor in determining its financial success and growth path. It has become essential for investors to comprehend how much a company relies on these foreign markets, as this understanding reveals the firm's potential for consistent earnings, its capacity to harness different economic cycles, and its overall growth prospects.

Being present in international markets serves as a counterbalance to domestic economic challenges while offering chances to engage with more rapidly evolving economies. However, this kind of diversification introduces challenges like currency fluctuations, geopolitical uncertainties and varying market trends.

Upon examining ABNB's recent quarterly performance, we noticed several interesting patterns in the revenue generated from its international segments, which are commonly analyzed and observed by Wall Street experts.

The company's total revenue for the quarter amounted to $4.87 billion, showing rise of 18.9%. We will now explore the breakdown of ABNB's overseas revenue to assess the impact of its international operations.

A Closer Look at ABNB's Revenue Streams Abroad

During the quarter, Asia Pacific contributed $323 million in revenue, making up 6.6% of the total revenue. When compared to the consensus estimate of $320 million, this meant a surprise of +0.94%. Looking back, Asia Pacific contributed $298 million, or 8.3%, in the previous quarter, and $272 million, or 6.6%, in the same quarter of the previous year.

Europe, the Middle East, and Africa accounted for 47.2% of the company's total revenue during the quarter, translating to $2.3 billion. Revenues from this region represented a surprise of -6.24%, with Wall Street analysts collectively expecting $2.45 billion. When compared to the preceding quarter and the same quarter in the previous year, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa contributed $1.43 billion (39.5%) and $1.97 billion (48.1%) to the total revenue, respectively.

Latin America generated $306 million in revenues for the company in the last quarter, constituting 6.3% of the total. This represented a surprise of +236.26% compared to the $91 million projected by Wall Street analysts. Comparatively, in the previous quarter, Latin America accounted for $291 million (8.1%), and in the year-ago quarter, it contributed $235 million (5.7%) to the total revenue.

Unity Software (U), Moderna (MRNA) and Airbnb (ABNB) stocks climbed to fresh 52-week highs on Monday, as strong earnings, upbeat revenue outlook and bullish analyst takes boosted investor sentiment. Unity benefited from its advertising business, Moderna returned to profit after two years, while Airbnb gained from improving growth prospects and Wall Street optimism.

Moderna and Airbnb stocks climbed 5% and 0.1%, respectively, while Unity stock pared gains and ended the session down 0.1%.

Unity's Growth Outlook Draws Wall Street Attention

Unity stock hit a four-year high of $54.27, extending its post-earnings rally after delivering a stronger-than-expected third quarter (Q3), with revenue increasing 32% year-on-year. The company also issued upbeat Q4 guidance, seeing strategic revenue growth of 65% to 67%. Its advertising and monetization business is expected to expand by an even faster 105% to 107%

Following the results, several analysts raised their price targets. Bank of America boosted its price target to $65 from $50 and kept a 'Buy' rating. Deutsche Bank raised its target to $70 from $50, suggesting a potential 36% upside from the stock's previous closing price.

CEO Matt Bromberg said that more developers using Unity's platform could help the company generate more advertising revenue. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment toward the stock remained 'extremely bullish'.

Moderna Gains As Analysts Express Optimism Around Cancer Vaccine

Moderna stock surged to a near five-year high of $280.80 after the company posted its first profitable quarter in two years. Q3 net income reached $162 million, or $0.38 per share, reversing a $200 million loss recorded a year earlier. Revenue advanced 29% to $1.31 billion, supported largely by stronger international sales of COVID-19 vaccines.

Piper Sandler raised its price target to $305 from $230 and kept an 'Overweight' rating, citing hopes for Moderna's experimental skin cancer vaccine developed with Merck. The firm expects a major regulatory development by 2027. Goldman Sachs also raised its price target to $195 after the strong earnings report and improved annual forecast.
